transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-29 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~38 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (QuantaForge Eng Mgr), Jamie Liu (QuantaForge Sr Backend), Rosa Delgado (QuantaForge ML)
Links shared: https://redwood.example.com/poc/quantaforge/logs (placeholder), https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/pocexample (repro spreadsheet)

Summary:
Quick POC sync to triage repeated mismatch between expected function/tool call payloads and structured JSON output from the SDK-instrumented runtime. Team suspects either SDK client serialization or backend preprocessor is altering requests; Redwood SE to reproduce. Discussed mitigation patterns (schema validation, tolerant parsers, canary routing to dedicated pool).

Topics:
- Repro timeline and frequency (intermittent, ~1 in 30 requests)
- Where mismatch appears: wrong field names, truncated arrays, extra wrapper object
- SDK v0.9.3 vs 0.9.5 behavior
- Streaming vs non-streaming responses and KV cache influence
- Acceptance criteria for POC success (stable structured output for 10k calls/day for 48h)

Action items (summarized): see metadata.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex Kim (AE): "All right folks, thanks for jumping on. Well try to keep this tight — 30 minutes ish. The goal is to triage the invoke mismatch you've been seeing. Priya from our side has the debug runbook. Samir, do you want to quickly restate what you're observing?"

[00:18] Samir Patel (QuantaForge): "Yeah, sure. Uh, thanks. So, in staging over the last week we've got this intermittent failure where a function call from the model returns structured JSON — the schema is off. Example: instead of sending `items: []` it sometimes comes back as `data: { items: [] }` or arrays are truncated. It happens on both streaming and non-streaming. Rate is low but it's blocking our downstream parser; our ETL just blows up. We captured a few payloads in the repro sheet."

[00:47] Priya Shah (SE): "Got it. Do you have an example request id? If you can drop one here that hits in the last 24 hours that'd help. Also, are you on SDK 0.9.3 or 0.9.5? We shipped a small serialization patch in .9.5 that's relevant to nested arrays."

[01:05] Jamie Liu (QuantaForge): "We're on 0.9.3 in staging still. We tried 0.9.5 locally and didn't reproduce right away; but the staging setup is slightly different, there's a gateway preprocessor. I can drop a failing request id — it's in the sheet, row 12."

[01:25] Rosa Delgado (ML): "To add, the model side logs show no hallucination; the model emits valid structure but by the time it reaches our parser it's different. So our suspicion is something during streaming chunk reassembly or a header being stripped."

[01:42] Priya Shah (SE): "Okay, that helps narrow it. A couple hypotheses: 1) client-side SDK streaming reassembly bug in 0.9.3; 2) gateway/proxy altering payload (content-type changes, chunk boundary issues); 3) our runtime KV cache returning a prefix that, under batching, misaligns arrays. We'll try to reproduce each. Priya: I'll take client logs and a deterministic replay; Alex will coordinate any routing changes."

[02:05] Alex Kim (AE): "Cool. Also quick commercial note: if you need dedicated routing to isolate for tests we can spin a small dedicated pool for the pilot — that helps rule out multi-tenant batching interactions. I'll send pricing for a short term, no long-term commit."

[02:25] Samir: "That might help if batching is the culprit. But we want to prioritize fixing the SDK path because many of our environments can't use dedicated."

[02:40] Priya: "Understood. We'll try to reproduce on both SaaS-hosted and a dedicated small pool. Samir, can you confirm the failing requests are reproducible with identical input? Is there any randomness in your prompt templates?"

[03:00] Samir: "There is some randomness in the prompt template — we append context fragments and sometimes a trailing comma gets inserted, but still, the model output is syntactically valid JSON in the logs. It just changes shape after transit."

[03:15] Jamie: "One thing we noticed: when responses stream, our gateway does some partial buffering and tries to re-chunk for downstream. If chunk boundaries align with structural tokens (like array brackets), partial reassembly could introduce duplicate wrappers. Not sure but plausible."

[03:40] Priya: "Good point. We'll instrument the gateway and the SDK at the same time. I want to note a recent fix in SDK .9.5 where we changed the chunk joiner to avoid inserting an extra newline — that could be correlated."

[04:00] Rosa: "Is there any way to detect when a wrapper has been added versus model-generated? We want alerts not just failures, so we can route to fallback parsing logic."

[04:12] Priya: "Yes — we can include a lightweight schema validation step client side; Redwood supports structured output validation hooks in the SDK that can run before the response is handed to your parser. That's in the examples folder; we'll point you to it. It will surface anomalies and can optionally request a re-fetch."

[04:35] Alex: "We'll share that example after the call. Also, Priya, can you capture the diffs between .9.3 and .9.5 chunking logic and log that as part of the repro?"

[04:50] Priya: "Yep. I'll attach a one-page note on differences and the test harness to the shared folder."

[05:05] Samir: "We also had an instance where arrays were truncated — only the first two elements made it through. That suggests maybe a streaming cutoff where the rest of the stream is dropped. Does Redwood have any request-level timeouts or max-chunk-size that could cause that?"

[05:22] Priya: "Default server-side token timeout is 60s for the hosted flow; but truncation at array boundaries can happen if the client closes the connection early or the gateway hits an intermediate TCP timeout. We'll look at server logs for connection resets around those request ids."

[05:40] Jamie: "Our gateway does have a 30s idle chunk timeout for reassembly. Could be the match. We'll try extending it."

[05:50] Rosa: "Are there known interactions with KV cache and structured output? I vaguely recall something where cached prefixes can duplicate top-level keys when the runtime merges KV cache and streaming outputs."

[06:05] Priya: "Yes, good memory. If you pin model variants and use prefix caching across requests, the runtime merges cached prefix tokens with generated tokens. Under some pathological batching patterns, a top-level wrapper could get introduced if the cache contains the wrapper from a previous prompt. We're going to test without prefix cache to rule that out."

[06:25] Alex: "To summarize technical plan: (1) Priya reproduces locally with SDK 0.9.3 & 0.9.5 and collects client logs; (2) Jamie extends gateway chunk timeout and provides exact failing request ids; (3) Samir exports model logs + request ids; (4) we test with caching disabled and with dedicated pool."

[06:45] Samir: "Sounds good. One more ask: can Redwood provide a small example harness we can run in our staging to validate streaming reassembly? We don't want to build it from scratch."

[06:55] Priya: "Yes — we have a streaming conformance harness. I'll drop it into the shared drive and include a short README. It includes a small Node and Python client runner that fakes chunk splits."

[07:10] Alex: "Great. Also let's talk acceptance criteria for the POC — Samir, you said earlier you wanted stability at 10k calls/day for 48 hours. Any other metrics?"

[07:22] Samir: "Latency must stay under 450ms P95 for simple invokes, and structured output error rate under 0.1% over the test window. Cost target is under $0.007 per 1k tokens. These are soft but if we hit them it's a buy signal."

[07:40] Priya: "Ok those are measurable. We'll help instrument p95 and error percentage in the Redwood Console and share a dashboard link."

[07:52] (brief crosstalk)

[08:05] Jamie: "I want to call out one oddity — sometimes the wrapper is an extra JSON object with a single key `payload` that contains the real structure. That looks like a proxy transformation more than a streaming bug."

[08:20] Priya: "Agreed. We'll inspect headers like `content-type` and `transfer-encoding` that could trigger middleware to wrap. Also check if the gateway has any body-parsing middleware enabled (some teams add a middleware that converts text/plain into JSON)."

[08:40] Rosa: "If the middleware is the issue, what's the recommended mitigation? Disable parsing? Force content-type?"

[08:50] Priya: "Force content-type to `application/octet-stream` or `text/event-stream` for streaming responses and add explicit pass-through rules in the gateway. We'll provide config snippets."

[09:05] Samir: "Ok I'll add that to our staging gateway next window."

[09:12] Alex: "Commercial aside: if you need RBAC or KMS integration during the pilot we can enable a scoped private deployment. But let's keep that as optional once the technicals are settled."

[09:25] Samir: "Not necessary yet, thanks. For now we want deterministic correctness."

[09:32] Priya: "All right, I'm going to run a few reproducibility steps live. I'm going to kick off a 1000-request run from SDK .9.3 with streaming enabled and log chunk boundaries. If you see a failing id I'll paste it in chat. Give me 6-8 minutes."

[09:48] (silence while Priya runs test)

[12:20] Priya: "Okay I have results — of 1k requests, I saw 2 anomalies that look similar: one had extra wrapper `payload`, another had truncated array. Request ids: r-4472 and r-4479. I'm uploading logs to the shared drive now. The anomalies occur when chunk boundary occurs at a close-brace token in the stream."

[12:45] Jamie: "Those ids match a staging failure we have. Good. I'll pull our gateway logs for those timestamps."

[12:52] Samir: "Anything in the logs that indicates the gateway re-chunked?"

[13:00] Jamie: "Yes, I see a 502-ish connector reset at r-4472 around 11:23:17. There's a re-open and the body gets re-posted — looks like our retry path sometimes wraps body in JSON when it re-posts."

[13:15] Priya: "That confirms middleware retry path is suspect. When a middleware performs a re-post it often serializes the body into a wrapper. We'll provide a diagnostic to detect that and instruct your gateway team."

[13:28] Rosa: "So then it's not a Redwood runtime bug, more of our gateway behavior?"

[13:34] Priya: "Likely in this case. But we'll still test with cache disabled and dedicated routing just to be thorough."

[13:45] Alex: "Given this, next steps are pretty straightforward. Priya uploads repro logs and harness. Jamie toggles gateway retry/serialization behavior and reruns the failing ids. Samir confirms parsing results. We'll reconvene if failures persist after 48h."

[14:02] Samir: "That timeline works. One small question on structured output validation — does Redwood's SDK support schema-based automatic re-fetch on mismatch or only alert?"

[14:15] Priya: "We have both. The SDK can run a JSON Schema validation and optionally perform an automated retry with a backoff. For POC we recommend alert+retry disabled while we root cause, then enable retry with a limit. We'll share config examples."

[14:30] Alex: "I'll also note that if you decide to accept a small error budget we can apply post-processing to patch known wrapper patterns — but that's a stopgap."

[14:45] (small laugh)

[14:50] Jamie: "Okay, I'll get the gateway team to run with retry serialization disabled and extend chunk timeout to 60s. We'll test overnight."

[15:00] Samir: "Priya, what's the ETA for the harness and the SDK diff note?"

[15:06] Priya: "I'll upload both in the next 24 hours — by 2026-12-30 EOD."

[15:12] Alex: "And I'll send a short note with optional dedicated pool pricing by 2027-01-07."

[15:20] Rosa: "Do we want another checkpoint next week? Same day/time?"

[15:25] Alex: "Let's shoot for 2027-01-05 15:00 UTC. If either side has confirmed fixes earlier we can cancel."

[15:32] Samir: "Works for me."

[15:36] Alex: "Okay great. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in the shared doc with logs and the harness."

[15:42] (meeting ends)
